text:
Arya: quick experiment heads-up: shifting KV cache granularity from per-seqBin -> per-session+seqBin for a canary build. want feedback on obvious pitfalls before i push prototype.

Devon: why session+seqBin? what tradeoffs are you targeting?

Arya: observed lots of prefix reuse inside a session (same user asking follow-ups) but sessions are short-lived. per-session keeps invalidation bounded on model reload while enabling intra-session reuse.

Sunil: watch out: driver rollouts currently clear whole namespace. introducing session keys without GC plan risks unbounded growth.

Luke: can we bake driver/model/version into the key prefix so incompatible keys become unreachable after bump? e.g. kv:v{drv_hash}:m{mid}:sess:{sid}:bin:{bin} 

Arya: yeah prototype key: `kv:v${driver_hash}:m${model_id}:sess:${session_id}:bin:${seq_bin}`. keeps keys reachable across quick restarts if driver_hash stable. flip by bumping driver_hash on major kernel changes.

ci-bot: perf-ci nightly: kv-cache-bench shows +1.1% p50 regression on gen-1 after enabling session keying (bench=bench-2026-03-10).

Luke: +1.1% p50. is the added latency from longer key sizes, more lookups, or persistence syscall overhead?

Arya: profiling points at metadata write path. we write metadata per-new-key to disk (fsync). longer keys also increase mem copy cost.

Devon: can we buffer metadata writes? we already do coalescing for kernel uploads. batching writes could amortize fsync.

Sunil: propose an in-memory journal layer: accept key writes into journal, flush every N ms or when size threshold hit. tradeoff: keys lost on crash but TTL+rehydration ok.

Arya: config knobs for prototype: `cache.keying.mode = "session_bin" | "global_bin"`, `cache.persistence.journal_flush_ms = 200`, `cache.persistence.atomic_writes = true|false`, `cache.ttl.session_default = 86400`.

Luke: add autotune policy: gather 7-day prefix-reuse histogram per model. if >60% reuse within session -> enable session_bin, else global_bin.

Arya: also must avoid heavy namespace scans for GC. plan: session TTL (24h) + async compactor job that scans by prefix and deletes old entries. no hot path scans.

Sunil: compactor job should be sharded and rate-limited to avoid impacting I/O. i'll prototype compactor with cursors and small batch deletes.

Arya: another perf note: average token latency dropped ~3.2% for chat workload (seqlen~32) due to better prefix hits, but overall p50 regressed in perf-ci because of write amplification on new keys.

Luke: suggest key header with kernel metadata hash so runtime won't reuse entries when kernel/layout changed: `kv:v${driver_hash}:m${model_id}:${kernel_meta_hash}:sess:${session_id}:bin:${seq_bin}`.

Arya: good idea. store small on-disk header per entry: `{model_id,kernel_meta_hash,seq_bin}` so compactor can do O(1) compatibility checks.

Devon: for persistence journaling: flush window should be autotuned by load. in low-load can be longer (500ms) to reduce fsyncs, under high-load shorten to preserve warm cache.

Sunil: need to cap per-session entries to avoid heavy-tail users: `cache.session.max_bins = 32`. also expose per-gpu caps to OOM-protect.

Arya: rollout plan: feature-flag behind `cache.keying.mode`, merge journal + tests, deploy canary 5% traffic, run nightly stress bench + trace hooks. revert if perf-ci >0.5% p50 regression.

ci-bot: reminder: add unit tests for key serialize/deserialize across driver/model/kernel bumps and a bench test matrix covering crash rehydrate path.

Luke: i'll add trace hooks for KV lookup latency and journal flush timers for canary.

Sunil: i'll size compactor and compaction windows. estimate per-GPU: 200k active sessions * avg 6 bins = 1.2M keys. avg key ~120B => ~144MB; journal ~50MB. need validation on machines with constrained RAM.

Arya: thanks. opening PR with feature flag, bench results attached. please review and comment in PR.

Devon: :thumbsup:

Sunil: scheduling infra sync tomorrow to discuss compactor I/O limits.

Arya: dropping follow-up notes in the PR. if anyone has edge-cases or objections post here or in PR.
